mock_data.title: Climate Change
mock_data.passage:
Experts in climatology and other scientists are becoming extremely concerned about the changes to our climate which are taking place. Admittedly, climate changes have occurred on our planet before. For example, there have been several ice ages or glacial periods.

These climatic changes, however, were different from the modern ones in that they occurred gradually and, as far as we know, naturally. The changes currently being monitored are said to be the result not of natural causes, but of human activity. Furthermore, the rate of change is becoming alarmingly rapid.

The major problem is that the planet appears to be warming up. According to some experts, this warming process, known as global warming, is occurring at a rate unprecedented in the last 10,000 years. The implications for the planet are very serious. Rising global temperatures could give rise to such ecological disasters as extremely high increases in the incidence of flooding and of droughts. These in turn could have a harmful effect on agriculture.

It is thought that this unusual warming of the Earth has been caused by so-called greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, being emitted into the atmosphere by car engines and modern industrial processes, for example. Such gases not only add to the pollution of the atmosphere, but also create a greenhouse effect, by which the heat of the sun is trapped. This leads to the warming up of the planet.

Politicians are also concerned about climate change and there are now regular summits on the subject, attended by representatives from around 180 of the world's industrialized countries. Of these summits, the most important took place in Kyoto in Japan in 1997. There it was agreed that the most industrialized countries would try to reduce the volume of greenhouse gas emissions and were given targets for this reduction of emissions.

It was also suggested that more forests should be planted to create so-called sinks to absorb greenhouse gases. At least part of the problem of rapid climate change has been caused by too drastic deforestation.

Sadly, the targets are not being met. Even more sadly, global warnings about climate changes are often still being regarded as scaremongering.
mock_data.passageB1:
Scientists who study the climate are worried about the changes happening to our planet. The climate is the usual weather in a place. Our climate is changing. In the past, the Earth's climate has changed. For example, there were times called ice ages when it was very cold.

But these old changes were different. They happened slowly and naturally. Today's changes are happening because of what people do. This is called human activity. Also, the changes are happening very quickly. This is a worrying sign.

The biggest problem is that the Earth is getting warmer. This is called global warming. Some scientists say the Earth is warming faster than it has in the last 10,000 years. This is very serious for the planet. Warmer temperatures can cause more flooding and droughts. Droughts are long periods without rain. These problems can hurt agriculture, which is farming.

The Earth is warming up because of gases in the air. These are called greenhouse gases. Cars and factories send these gases into the air. One of these gases is carbon dioxide. These gases pollute the air. They also trap heat from the sun. This is called the greenhouse effect. The greenhouse effect makes the planet warmer.

Politicians are also worried about climate change. They have meetings to talk about it. People from about 180 countries go to these meetings. An important meeting was in Kyoto, Japan, in 1997. There, countries agreed to try to reduce the amount of greenhouse gases they send into the air. They were given goals to reduce these gases.

They also said we should plant more trees. Trees can absorb greenhouse gases. Cutting down too many trees, called deforestation, has made climate change worse.

Sadly, countries are not meeting their goals. Even worse, some people still think that warnings about climate change are just trying to scare people (scaremongering).
mock_data.passageB2:
Scientists who study the climate are becoming increasingly worried about the changes happening to our planet's climate. It's true that the Earth's climate has changed before. For instance, we know there have been several ice ages in the past.

However, these past climate shifts were different from what's happening now. They occurred slowly and, as far as we understand, due to natural processes. The changes we're seeing today are believed to be caused by human activities, not natural ones. What's more, the speed of these changes is becoming alarmingly fast.

The main concern is that the Earth seems to be getting warmer. Some experts say this warming, known as global warming, is happening faster than at any time in the last 10,000 years. This has serious implications for the planet. Rising temperatures could lead to ecological disasters, like a big increase in floods and droughts. These events could then negatively affect farming and food production.

It's thought that this unusual warming is caused by greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide. These gases are released into the atmosphere by things like car engines and modern factories. These gases not only pollute the air but also create a 'greenhouse effect'. This means they trap the sun's heat, leading to the planet warming up. Deforestation also contributes to the problem, as trees absorb greenhouse gases.

Politicians are also concerned about climate change, and there are regular international meetings, or summits, on the topic. Representatives from many of the world's industrialized countries attend these. One of the most important summits took place in Kyoto, Japan, in 1997. There, it was agreed that industrialized countries should try to reduce their emissions of greenhouse gases and were given specific goals to achieve this reduction. Measures like planting more forests were suggested to absorb greenhouse gases.

Unfortunately, the agreed targets are often not being met. Even more concerning is that warnings about climate change are still often dismissed as exaggeration or scaremongering. This lack of action poses a significant threat to our planet's future and requires immediate attention.
mock_data.passageC1:
The escalating alterations to our planet's climate are causing considerable disquiet among climatologists and other scientific experts. While it is undeniable that climatic shifts have punctuated Earth's history, evidenced by recurring ice ages or glacial epochs, the current transformations are distinct.

These historical fluctuations differed fundamentally from contemporary trends, primarily because they unfolded over extended geological timescales and, to the best of our understanding, arose from natural processes. By contrast, the changes we are presently observing are widely attributed to anthropogenic activities, and, perhaps more alarmingly, the rate of change is demonstrating an unprecedented acceleration.

The central concern revolves around the discernible warming of the planet. This phenomenon, commonly referred to as global warming, is, according to numerous experts, progressing at a rate unparalleled in the preceding ten millennia. The far-reaching implications for the planet are severe. Elevated global temperatures could precipitate ecological catastrophes, such as a dramatic surge in the frequency and intensity of both floods and droughts. Such events would inevitably exert a detrimental influence on agricultural productivity and global food security.

The prevailing scientific consensus attributes this anomalous warming to the increased concentrations of greenhouse gases, notably carbon dioxide, released into the atmosphere by sources such as vehicle emissions and industrial processes. These gases not only contribute to atmospheric pollution but also create a 'greenhouse effect', effectively trapping solar radiation and thereby elevating planetary temperatures. The insidious nature of this process demands immediate attention.

Politicians are also increasingly cognizant of the gravity of climate change, as evidenced by the regular international summits convened to address this issue, bringing together representatives from approximately 180 industrialized nations. The Kyoto Protocol, established in 1997, represents a landmark agreement, wherein industrialized nations pledged to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions and were assigned specific reduction targets. The success of these summits hinges on the commitment of each nation.

Furthermore, proposals have been put forth to expand forest cover, establishing 'carbon sinks' to sequester atmospheric greenhouse gases. Indeed, excessive deforestation has, to a significant extent, exacerbated the problem of accelerated climate change. Regrettably, many nations are failing to meet their agreed-upon targets. More concerningly, warnings regarding the perils of climate change are still frequently dismissed as mere scaremongering, a viewpoint that serves only to impede progress towards effective mitigation strategies.

mock_data.translation:
Klimatologiya mutaxassislari va boshqa olimlar bizning iqlimimizda sodir bo'layotgan o'zgarishlar haqida haddan tashqari tashvishlanmoqdalar. Tan olish kerakki, iqlim o'zgarishlari sayyoramizda ilgari ham yuz bergan. Masalan, bir nechta muzlik davrlari yoki glazial davrlar bo'lgan.

Biroq, bu iqlim o'zgarishlari zamonaviylaridan farq qilgan, chunki ular asta-sekin va biz bilganimizdek, tabiiy ravishda sodir bo'lgan. Hozirda kuzatilayotgan o'zgarishlar tabiiy sabablar bilan emas, balki insoniyat faoliyati bilan bog'liq deyiladi. Bundan tashqari, o'zgarish sur'ati xavotirli darajada tez bo'lib bormoqda.

Asosiy muammo shundaki, sayyoramiz isinib borayotganga o'xshaydi. Ba'zi mutaxassislarga ko'ra, global isish deb nomlanuvchi bu isish jarayoni so'nggi 10,000 yilda misli ko'rilmagan sur'atda sodir bo'lmoqda. Bunning sayyora uchun oqibatlari juda jiddiy. Global haroratning ko'tarilishi suv toshqini va qurg'oqchilik hodisalarining haddan tashqari ko'payishi kabi ekologik falokatlarni keltirib chiqarishi mumkin. Bular o'z navbatida qishloq xo'jaligiga zararli ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin.

Yerning bu g'ayrioddiy isishiga issiqxona gazlari, masalan, karbonat angidrid deb ataladigan gazlar sabab bo'lgan deb hisoblanadi, bu gazlar avtomobil dvigatellari va zamonaviy sanoat jarayonlari orqali atmosferaga chiqariladi. Bunday gazlar nafaqat atmosfera ifloslanishini kuchaytiradi, balki quyosh issiqligini tuzoqqa tushiradigan issiqxona effektini ham yaratadi. Bu sayyoraning isishiga olib keladi.

Siyosatchilar ham iqlim o'zgarishi haqida tashvishlanmoqdalar va hozirda bu mavzuda muntazam sammitlar o'tkazilmoqda, ularda dunyoning taxminan 180 ta sanoati rivojlangan mamlakatlari vakillari qatnashmoqda. Bu sammitlarning eng muhimi 1997 yilda Yaponiyaning Kioto shahrida bo'lib o'tdi. U yerda eng ko'p sanoatlashgan mamlakatlar issiqxona gazi chiqindilarini kamaytirishga harakat qilishlari va bu chiqindilarni kamaytirish uchun maqsadlar berilishi kelishib olindi.

Shuningdek, issiqxona gazlarini so'rib olish uchun absorbent deb ataladigan narsalarni yaratish uchun ko'proq o'rmonlar ekish kerakligi taklif qilindi. Tez iqlim o'zgarishi muammosining kamida bir qismi haddan tashqari o'rmonlarni kesish bilan bog'liq.

Afsuski, maqsadlarga erishilmayapti. Yanada afsuski, iqlim o'zgarishi haqidagi global ogohlantirishlar hali ham ko'pincha vahima tarqatish deb hisoblanadi.

mock_data.translationB1:
Iqlimni oʻrganuvchi olimlar sayyoramizda sodir boʻlayotgan oʻzgarishlardan xavotirda. Iqlim – bu bir joydagi odatiy ob-havo. Bizning iqlimimiz oʻzgarmoqda. Oʻtmishda Yerning iqlimi oʻzgargan. Masalan, juda sovuq boʻlgan muzlik davrlari boʻlgan.

Lekin bu eski oʻzgarishlar boshqacha edi. Ular sekin va tabiiy ravishda sodir boʻlgan. Bugungi oʻzgarishlar odamlarning harakatlari tufayli sodir boʻlmoqda. Bu inson faoliyati deb ataladi. Shuningdek, oʻzgarishlar juda tez sodir boʻlmoqda. Bu xavotirli belgi.

Eng katta muammo – Yerning isishi. Bu global isish deb ataladi. Ba'zi olimlarning aytishicha, Yer soʻnggi 10 000 yildagidan ham tezroq isimoqda. Bu sayyora uchun juda jiddiy. Iliq haroratlar koʻproq suv toshqinlari va qurgʻoqchiliklarga olib kelishi mumkin. Qurgʻoqchiliklar – yomgʻirsiz uzoq davrlar. Bu muammolar qishloq xoʻjaligiga, yaʼni dehqonchilikka zarar yetkazishi mumkin.

Yer havoda gazlar borligi sababli isimoqda. Bular issiqxona gazlari deb ataladi. Avtomobillar va fabrikalar bu gazlarni havoga chiqaradi. Bu gazlardan biri karbonat angidriddir. Bu gazlar havoni ifloslantiradi. Ular, shuningdek, quyoshdan keladigan issiqlikni ushlab qoladi. Bu issiqxona effekti deb ataladi. Issiqxona effekti sayyorani isitadi.

Siyosatchilar ham iqlim oʻzgarishidan xavotirda. Ular bu haqda gaplashish uchun yigʻilishlar oʻtkazadilar. Bu yigʻilishlarga taxminan 180 ta davlatdan odamlar boradi. Muhim yigʻilish 1997-yilda Yaponiyaning Kioto shahrida boʻlib oʻtdi. U yerda davlatlar havoga chiqaradigan issiqxona gazlari miqdorini kamaytirishga kelishib oldilar. Ularga bu gazlarni kamaytirish boʻyicha maqsadlar berildi.

Ular, shuningdek, koʻproq daraxt ekishimiz kerakligini aytishdi. Daraxtlar issiqxona gazlarini yutishi mumkin. Juda koʻp daraxt kesish, yaʼni oʻrmonlarning yoʻq qilinishi iqlim oʻzgarishini yanada yomonlashtirdi.

Afsuski, davlatlar oʻz maqsadlariga erisha olmayapti. Bundan ham yomoni, ba'zi odamlar hali ham iqlim oʻzgarishi haqidagi ogohlantirishlar shunchaki odamlarni qoʻrqitishga urinish (vahima qoʻzgʻash) deb oʻylashadi.

Iqlimni o'rganuvchi olimlar sayyoramiz iqlimida sodir bo'layotgan o'zgarishlardan tobora ko'proq xavotirda. Haqiqatan ham, Yer iqlimi ilgari ham o'zgargan. Misol uchun, biz o'tmishda bir nechta muzlik davrlari bo'lganini bilamiz.

Biroq, bu o'tmishdagi iqlim o'zgarishlari hozir sodir bo'layotganidan farq qilgan. Ular sekin-asta va biz tushunganimizdek, tabiiy jarayonlar tufayli yuz bergan. Bugungi kunda ko'rayotgan o'zgarishlar tabiiy emas, balki inson faoliyati natijasida yuzaga keladi, deb ishoniladi. Bundan tashqari, bu o'zgarishlarning tezligi vahimali darajada tezlashmoqda.

Asosiy xavotir shundaki, Yer isib borayotganga o'xshaydi. Ba'zi ekspertlarning ta'kidlashicha, global isish deb nomlanuvchi bu isish so'nggi 10 000 yil ichida har qanday vaqtdagidan tezroq sodir bo'lmoqda. Bu sayyora uchun jiddiy oqibatlarga olib keladi. Haroratning ko'tarilishi toshqinlar va qurg'oqchilikning sezilarli darajada oshishi kabi ekologik falokatlarga olib kelishi mumkin. Bu hodisalar keyinchalik dehqonchilik va oziq-ovqat ishlab chiqarishga salbiy ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin.

Taxminlarga ko'ra, bu g'ayrioddiy isish issiqxona gazlari, masalan, karbonat angidrid tufayli yuzaga keladi. Bu gazlar avtomobil dvigatellari va zamonaviy fabrikalar kabi narsalar orqali atmosferaga chiqariladi. Bu gazlar nafaqat havoni ifloslantiradi, balki "issiqxona effektini" ham yaratadi. Bu shuni anglatadiki, ular quyosh issiqligini ushlab qoladi, bu esa sayyoraning isishiga olib keladi. O'rmonlarning kesilishi ham muammoga hissa qo'shadi, chunki daraxtlar issiqxona gazlarini yutadi.

Siyosatchilar ham iqlim o'zgarishidan xavotirda va bu mavzu bo'yicha muntazam xalqaro uchrashuvlar yoki sammitlar bo'lib o'tadi. Ushbu uchrashuvlarda dunyoning ko'plab sanoatlashgan mamlakatlari vakillari ishtirok etadi. Eng muhim sammitlardan biri 1997 yilda Yaponiyaning Kioto shahrida bo'lib o'tdi. U erda sanoatlashgan mamlakatlar issiqxona gazlari emissiyasini kamaytirishga harakat qilishlari va bu kamayishga erishish uchun aniq maqsadlar berilganligi kelishib olindi. Issiqxona gazlarini yutish uchun ko'proq o'rmonlar ekish kabi chora-tadbirlar taklif etildi.

Afsuski, kelishilgan maqsadlarga ko'pincha erishilmayapti. Bundan ham tashvishlisi shundaki, iqlim o'zgarishi haqidagi ogohlantirishlar ko'pincha mubolag'a yoki vahima qo'zg'ash sifatida rad etiladi. Bu harakatsizlik sayyoramiz kelajagiga jiddiy tahdid soladi va zudlik bilan e'tibor talab etadi.

Sayyoramiz iqlimidagi tobora kuchayib borayotgan o'zgarishlar iqlimshunoslar va boshqa ilmiy mutaxassislar orasida katta tashvish uyg'otmoqda. Yer tarixida iqlim o'zgarishlari, takrorlanuvchi muzlik davrlari yoki muzlik davrlari bilan isbotlanganidek, bo'lgani inkor etib bo'lmasa-da, hozirgi o'zgarishlar o'ziga xosdir.

Bu tarixiy tebranishlar zamonaviy tendentsiyalardan tubdan farq qiladi, asosan, ular uzoq geologik vaqt oralig'ida yuz berganligi va bizning tushunchamizga ko'ra, tabiiy jarayonlardan kelib chiqqanligi sababli. Aksincha, biz hozir kuzatayotgan o'zgarishlar keng tarqalgan holda antropogen faoliyat bilan bog'liq va, ehtimol, yanada xavotirli tomoni shundaki, o'zgarish tezligi misli ko'rilmagan tezlashuvni namoyish etmoqda.

Asosiy xavotir sayyoramizning sezilarli darajada isishi bilan bog'liq. Odatda global isish deb ataladigan bu hodisa, ko'plab ekspertlarning fikriga ko'ra, o'tgan o'n ming yillikda misli ko'rilmagan tezlikda rivojlanmoqda. Sayyora uchun keng qamrovli oqibatlar juda jiddiy. Global haroratning oshishi ekologik falokatlarga, masalan, suv toshqinlari va qurg'oqchilikning chastotasi va intensivligining keskin oshishiga olib kelishi mumkin. Bunday hodisalar, albatta, qishloq xo'jaligi mahsuldorligiga va global oziq-ovqat xavfsizligiga salbiy ta'sir ko'rsatadi.

Ilmiy kelishuv bu anomaliyalik isishni issiqxona gazlarining, xususan, karbonat angidridning, avtomobil chiqindilari va sanoat jarayonlari kabi manbalar tomonidan atmosferaga chiqarilishi bilan bog'laydi. Bu gazlar nafaqat atmosfera ifloslanishiga hissa qo'shadi, balki "issiqxona effekti"ni ham yaratadi, quyosh radiatsiyasini samarali ravishda ushlab turadi va shu bilan sayyora haroratini oshiradi. Bu jarayonning yashirin tabiati zudlik bilan e'tibor talab qiladi.

Siyosatchilar ham iqlim o'zgarishining jiddiyligini tobora anglab yetmoqdalar, buning dalili sifatida bu masalani hal qilish uchun muntazam ravishda xalqaro sammitlar o'tkazilmoqda, ularda taxminan 180 ta sanoatlashgan davlat vakillari ishtirok etmoqda. 1997 yilda tuzilgan Kioto protokoli muhim kelishuv bo'lib, unda sanoatlashgan davlatlar issiqxona gazlari emissiyasini kamaytirishga va'da berishdi va ularga aniq kamaytirish maqsadlari belgilandi. Bu sammitlarning muvaffaqiyati har bir davlatning majburiyatiga bog'liq.

Bundan tashqari, atmosfera issiqxona gazlarini ajratib olish uchun "uglerod havzalari"ni yaratish, o'rmon qoplamini kengaytirish bo'yicha takliflar ilgari surildi. Haqiqatan ham, haddan tashqari o'rmonlarning kesilishi, sezilarli darajada, iqlim o'zgarishining tezlashuvi muammoni yanada kuchaytirdi. Afsuski, ko'plab davlatlar kelishilgan maqsadlariga erisha olmayapti. Eng tashvishlisi shundaki, iqlim o'zgarishining xavfi haqidagi ogohlantirishlar hali ham ko'pincha shunchaki qo'rqitish sifatida rad etiladi, bu nuqtai nazar samarali yumshatish strategiyalari sari rivojlanishga to'sqinlik qiladi, xolos.
